items: notes read [key] — read a note; without a key, read the root bootstrap note.
notes list — list all note keys.
notes load -d <key> <file> — load JSON from a file; -d deletes the local file after successful load.
notes delete <key> — delete a note; follow the conservative maintenance rules before deleting potentially referenced content.

para: Choose the workflow by interface. MCP: fetch current revision, then patch/batch for targeted edits or put for a structural rewrite. CLI: create/edit a local JSON file and use notes load. Preserve metadata and links, increment version, update the date, then read back. See
When updating an existing note: read it first, preserve all content and links, increment
Current block types: para, heading, codeblock, list, table, image, svg, details and section. Authoritative grammar and compatibility are in

Lists use {list: {items: [...], ordered?: boolean, label?: string}}. Canonical items are strings or inline arrays; legacy record objects are compatibility forms. Use explicit link objects for portable links; automatic path linking differs between consumers.
• Index notes link to children; children link back up to parent
• CONTENTS must be updated whenever a new note subtree is created — orphaned notes are invisible to Envoy
• Version + date on every update; never append-only
• Semantic organisation by topic, not chronological
• No note is an island — always link up after creating

~/py/envoy/jsonhtl_to_html.py — static exporter using the shared renderer.
